extracted.intended_audience: writers, dramatists, storytellers, and students of narratology
extracted.subtask_description: A catalog of 36 dramatic situation types (from Georges Polti) used as a tool for generating, categorizing, or analyzing plots and scenes in stories, plays, and films. Each entry lists the required dramatic elements and gives brief descriptions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplication
rubrics_metrics.description: a persecutor; a suppliant; a power in authority, whose decision is doubtful. The suppliant appeals to the power in authority for deliverance from the persecutor. The power in authority may be a distinct person or merely an attribute of the persecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Esther interceding to the king on behalf of the Jews for deliverance from the king's chief advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverance
rubrics_metrics.description: an unfortunate; a threatener; a rescuer. The unfortunate has caused a conflict, and the threatener is to carry out justice, but the rescuer saves the unfortunate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Ifigenia in Tauride; Superman (1941 film).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime pursued by vengeance
rubrics_metrics.description: a criminal; an avenger. The criminal commits a crime that will not see justice, so the avenger seeks justice by punishing the criminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Count of Monte Cristo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vengeance taken for kin upon kin
rubrics_metrics.description: Guilty Kinsman; an Avenging Kinsman; remembrance of the Victim, a relative of both. Two entities, the Guilty and the Avenging Kinsmen, are put into conflict over wrongdoing to the Victim, who is allied to both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: punishment; a fugitive. The fugitive flees punishment for a misunderstood conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster
rubrics_metrics.description: a vanquished power; a victorious enemy or a messenger. The vanquished power falls from their place after being defeated by the victorious enemy or being informed of such a defeat by the messenger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falling prey to cruelty/misfortune
rubrics_metrics.description: an unfortunate; a master or a misfortune. The unfortunate suffers from misfortune and/or at the hands of the master.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revolt
rubrics_metrics.description: a tyrant; a conspirator. The tyrant, a cruel power, is plotted against by the conspirator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daring enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: a bold leader; an object; an adversary. The bold leader takes the object from the adversary by overpowering the adversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Queste del Saint Graal; The Lord of the Rings; Raiders of the Lost Ark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abduction
rubrics_metrics.description: an abductor; the abducted; a guardian. The abductor takes the abducted from the guardian.

rubrics_metrics.name: The enigma
rubrics_metrics.description: a problem; an interrogator; a seeker. The interrogator poses a problem to the seeker and gives a seeker better ability to reach the seeker's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining
rubrics_metrics.description: (a Solicitor & an adversary who is refusing) or (an arbitrator & opposing parties). The solicitor is at odds with the adversary who refuses to give the solicitor an object in the possession of the adversary, or an arbitrator decides who gets the object desired by opposing parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enmity of kin
rubrics_metrics.description: a Malevolent Kinsman; a Hated or a reciprocally-hating Kinsman. The Malevolent Kinsman and the Hated or a second Malevolent Kinsman conspire together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rivalry of kin
rubrics_metrics.description: the Preferred Kinsman; the Rejected Kinsman; the Object of Rivalry. The Object of Rivalry chooses the Preferred Kinsman over the Rejected Kinsman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Murderous adultery
rubrics_metrics.description: two Adulterers; a Betrayed Spouse. Two Adulterers conspire to kill the Betrayed Spouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madness
rubrics_metrics.description: a Madman; a Victim. The Madman goes insane and wrongs the Victim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatal imprudence
rubrics_metrics.description: the Imprudent; a Victim or an Object Lost. The Imprudent, by neglect or ignorance, loses the Object Lost or wrongs the Victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Kris Kelvin and his wife in Solaris (1972 film).

rubrics_metrics.name: Involuntary crimes of love
rubrics_metrics.description: a Lover; a Beloved; a Revealer. The Lover and the Beloved have unknowingly broken a taboo through their romantic relationship, and the Revealer reveals this to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Oedipus, Jocasta and the messenger from Corinth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slaying of kin unrecognized
rubrics_metrics.description: the Slayer; an Unrecognized Victim. The Slayer kills the Unrecognized Victim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-sacrifice for an ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: a Hero; an Ideal; a Creditor or a Person/Thing sacrificed. The Hero sacrifices the Person or Thing for their Ideal, which is then taken by the Creditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-sacrifice for kin
rubrics_metrics.description: a Hero; a Kinsman; a Creditor or a Person/Thing sacrificed. The Hero sacrifices a Person or Thing for their Kinsman, which is then taken by the Creditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: All sacrificed for passion
rubrics_metrics.description: a Lover; an Object of fatal Passion; the Person/Thing sacrificed. A Lover sacrifices a Person or Thing for the Object of their Passion, which is then lost forever.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of sacrificing loved ones
rubrics_metrics.description: a Hero; a Beloved Victim; the Necessity for the Sacrifice. The Hero wrongs the Beloved Victim because of the Necessity for their Sacrifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rivalry of superior vs. inferior
rubrics_metrics.description: a Superior Rival; an Inferior Rival; the Object of Rivalry. An Inferior Rival bests a Superior Rival and wins the Object of Rivalry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adultery
rubrics_metrics.description: two Adulterers; a Deceived Spouse. Two Adulterers conspire against the Deceived Spouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crimes of love
rubrics_metrics.description: a Lover; the Beloved. A Lover and the Beloved break a taboo by initiating a romantic relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Sigmund and his sister in The Valkyrie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of the dishonour of a loved one
rubrics_metrics.description: a Discoverer; the Guilty One. The Discoverer discovers the wrongdoing committed by the Guilty One.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstacles to love
rubrics_metrics.description: two Lovers; an Obstacle. Two Lovers face an Obstacle together.

rubrics_metrics.name: An enemy loved
rubrics_metrics.description: a Lover; the Beloved Enemy; the Hater. The allied Lover and Hater have diametrically opposed attitudes towards the Beloved Enemy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: an Ambitious Person; a Thing Coveted; an Adversary. The Ambitious Person seeks the Thing Coveted and is opposed by the Adversary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict with a god
rubrics_metrics.description: a Mortal; an Immortal. The Mortal and the Immortal enter a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistaken jealousy
rubrics_metrics.description: a Jealous One; an Object of whose Possession He is Jealous; a Supposed Accomplice; a Cause or an Author of the Mistake. The Jealous One falls victim to the Cause or the Author of the Mistake and becomes jealous of the Object and becomes conflicted with the Supposed Accomplice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erroneous judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: a Mistaken One; a Victim of the Mistake; a Cause or Author of the Mistake; the Guilty One. The Mistaken One falls victim to the Cause or the Author of the Mistake and passes judgment against the Victim of the Mistake when it should be passed against the Guilty One instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remorse
rubrics_metrics.description: a Culprit; a Victim or the Sin; an Interrogator. The Culprit wrongs the Victim or commits the Sin, and is at odds with the Interrogator who seeks to understand the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of a lost one
rubrics_metrics.description: a Seeker; the One Found. The Seeker finds the One Found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A Very Long Engagement; Finding Nemo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of loved ones
rubrics_metrics.description: a Kinsman Slain; a Kinsman Spectator; an Executioner. The killing of the Kinsman Slain by the Executioner is witnessed by the Kinsman.
